brief: A planter for a sunny kitchen windowsill with three herbs growing in it.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.requirement: Planter for kitchen windowsill (compact, linear form to fit sill)
requirements.evidence: 3 cells in line at q -1,0 / 0,0 / 1,0 (pieces piece:-1,0,0;full, piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full) with 3 full-depth bins (bin:-1,0,0, bin:0,0,0, bin:1,0,0) ~529mm long x 177mm deep, suitable for narrow windowsill. Caps and joint bolts fitted.
Open-top bins with soil allow full sun exposure; no shade structures. Material/UV resistance not verified by configurator – shape helps by being low and open.
Three bins filled with soil and planted: basil-harvest in bin:-1,0,0, mint-harvest in bin:0,0,0, parsley-harvest in bin:1,0,0 (props 1-3 visible in look).

finish.summary: Linear 3-cell windowsill planter with three full bins, each filled with soil and planted with a different herb (basil, mint, parsley). Open tops maximise sun, compact footprint fits sill, caps and joint bolts applied.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Your sunny windowsill herb planter — I'll set it up for three fresh herbs.
